Subject: Dedicated top-up / burst policy clarification

Karthik —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Two implementation questions came up from our infra and SRE teams as we plan the Q4 migration:

1) When we hit an unexpected traffic spike during our import window, what is the hard limit on burst capacity per GPU pool and how is it billed (per-minute slab vs per-token)?
2) Are cooldown exceptions available for one-off migrations (we're planning a 72-hour ingest in Oct) or will the standard 4-week cooldown apply?

We're close on the committed GPUs and just need clarity on the top-up piece before legal signs off. I attached the traffic projection so you can see expected peaks.

—Jordan
Acme Cloud — Head of Platform
attachments: traffic-projection-acme-aug2026.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Aisha Kumari <aisha.k@acmecloud.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 20:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated top-up / burst policy clarification

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear questions and the projection. Summary answers up top, details below: 

Quick answers:
- Hard burst limit: configurable per-pool; standard offer is 2.5x committed throughput for up to 6 hours/day.
- Billing: burst minutes are billed on a per-minute metered rate with a 15-minute minimum slab; we can alternatively offer a prepaid credit slab for predictable monthly usage.
- Cooldown exceptions: we can grant a one-time short-duration exception (up to 7 days) for migration events with a signed MA/SoW and a nominal surcharge.

Detailed notes:
1) Limits and fiscal treatment
- Default: Dedicated pool has a peak multiplier (2.5x) to preserve headroom and latency SLOs. Anything above that is treated as surge and billed at the surge rate. The surge rate is expressed as a multiplier of the committed unit price (default 3.0x). Billing granularity is per-minute after the 15-minute floor.
- Option: If you want tighter cost predictability, we can offer a Top-up slab (prepaid credits measured in GPU-minute equivalents) at a discounted blended rate vs pure surge billing. That slab can be sized to your projection and consumed before surge kicks in.

2) Cooldown and exceptions
- Standard cooldown: 4-week cooldown between significant burst activations per pool to avoid persistent overcommit.
- Exception: For migration windows we can grant a 72-hour to 7-day exception if you agree to an addendum that documents the window and either (a) pays the standard surge multiplier, or (b) purchases a one-off prepaid slab that qualifies for a 10-15% discount to the surge rate.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll draft a short addendum (v3 attached) with two options: Surge-billed exception or Prepaid Top-up slab.
- If you prefer the slab, let me know a target monthly GPU-minute quantity and we will model pricing.

Sending to Marissa and Monica to confirm commercial/discount flexibility for an annual commit.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: RDW_Dedicated_TopUp_Addendum_v3.pdf (draft addendum)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, monica_patel@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -04:00
Subject: FW: Dedicated top-up / burst policy clarification — Acme (RDW-2134)

Marissa / Monica —

Acme is asking for a migration exception (72-hour window, likely Oct). They are finalizing an annual committed pool but need the top-up behavior locked. I recommended two commercial paths:

A) Surge exception: allow 2.5x peak for up to 7 days; bill excess at 3.0x committed unit price.
B) Prepaid Top-up slab: customer prepays a block of GPU-minutes at ~1.6x committed price (blended) that would be consumed before surge billing.

They've shared traffic projections (attached). Their signal is: they'd take the annual commit if we can either: reduce the surge multiplier to 2.6x for the migration window, or provide a 12–15% discount on the prepaid slab.

Requesting guidance: what flexibility do we have on the surge multiplier and slab discount for an ARR/Committed spend in the mid-six figures? Also confirm whether legal needs specific language around rollback to standard cooldown after the migration.

Thanks — quick turnaround would be great, they want this in the MSA addendum by next week.

—Karthik

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, monica_patel@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 10:07:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: FW: Dedicated top-up / burst policy clarification — Acme (RDW-2134)

Karthik —

We can do a constrained commercial exception for this customer given the committed spend. Guidance:

- Surge multiplier: approve reduction to 2.6x for the documented migration window (max 7 days). This must be a one-time, non-recurring exception and spelled out in the addendum.
- Prepaid slab discount: approve up to 12% off the standard surge rate for a prepaid GPU-minute slab sized to their projection. Anything deeper needs VP approval.
- Cooldown: include clause that enforces the standard 4-week cooldown after the migration window; emergency read-only exceptions require CISO sign-off.
- Billing/failure mode: if the slab is exhausted early, additional usage will default to 3.0x surge rate. Add a soft cap notification rule (email + paging) when they hit 80% of slab.

Marissa — VP, Sales Ops.

Cc: Monica — please coordinate with Legal/Sales-Strategic to get the addendum language tightened. Once Legal confirms, Karthik can present both options to Acme.

—Marissa
